headline: ServiceNow's president publicly denied that the company plans to buy the AI customer-service startup Decagon, and its shares rose about 5%.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a clear on-record denial with a share-price reaction, but it adds no new deal.
importance_line: Matters mainly to ServiceNow shareholders and to Decagon, whose reported search for a buyer is not answered by the denial, which rules out ServiceNow only.
summary: 24/7 Wall St. reports that Amit Zavery, ServiceNow's president, chief product officer and chief operating officer, said on 14 Oct 2026 that ServiceNow "has no interest or intention of purchasing Decagon", a maker of AI customer-service agents, and that it prioritizes organic growth; its shares rose about 5% in midday trading on 15 Oct 2026. This follows a Business Insider report of 14 Oct 2026 that Decagon had held early talks about a sale and hired a banker, though the article read does not say that report named ServiceNow.
notes: Continues the 14 Oct Decagon M&A story; new today is ServiceNow's denial.
